To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Nf1-deficient cells exhibit a transcriptional signature of a stem/progenitor phenotype, which is consistent with the observation that Nf1-deficiency leads to the formation of MPNSTs that are highly invasive and have the potential to metastasize.

(1) Nf1 deficiency leads to the upregulation of the transcription factor ETS2 in MPNST; (2) the ETS2 transcription factor is a key downstream effector in MPNSTs and that (3) ETS2 is a promising therapeutic target for MPNSTs.

1) Nf1 deficiency in MPNST cells induces a significant increase of the transcriptional factor ETS2 and its target genes, which are associated with tumor cell proliferation and migration; and 2) Nf1 deficient MPNST cells have increased sensitivity to the inhibition of ETS2 transcriptional activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the transcriptional mechanisms downstream and/or parallel to the Nf1/RAS/MAPK pathway in MPNSTs.
the identification of novel transcriptional pathways downstream of Nf1 deficiency in MPNSTs and the characterization of their roles in tumorigenesis.
the identification of novel therapeutic targets downstream of RAS/MAPK in MPNSTs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this dissertation work identified the transcriptional mechanisms downstream to NF1 deficiency in MPNSTs and provided evidence that the transcriptional regulation by NF1 deficiency may contribute to the pathogenesis of MPNSTs.

Nf1 deficiency leads to a transcriptional reprogramming that is associated with MPNST development and that this transcriptional reprogramming is associated with the expression of genes that are involved in the regulation of the cell cycle and the maintenance of the cell cycle.
the Nf1 mutation leads to the activation of RAS-MAPK pathway in MPNSTs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we identified the transcriptional mechanisms downstream to Nf1 deficiency in MPNSTs.
we identified a number of transcriptional mechanisms that are regulated by neurofibromin in MPNSTs.

we have identified a number of transcriptional changes in MPNSTs compared to normal human peripheral nerve tissue, and that we have identified the transcription factor, NF-Y, as a potential target in NF1-associated MPNSTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional response of MPNSTs in the absence of neurofibromin is a complex and dynamic process, involving the coordinated regulation of multiple transcription factors.
the Nf1 deficiency leads to a transcriptional program that is different in NF1 and sporadic MPNSTs.
Nf1-deficient MPNSTs are transcriptionally dysregulated and the dysregulated genes are enriched in the MAPK pathway.
